studies.comparison_type: per 20 nmol/L decrease [inverted ⇒ high vs low]
studies.evidence_locator: The estimated odds ratio for high-grade serous epithelial ovarian cancer (4121 cases) was 1.54 (1.19, 2.01) per 20 nmol/L decrease in 25(OH)D concentration; inverted for high versus low vitamin D.
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: We employed SNPs with well-established associations with 25(OH)D concentration as instrumental variables for MR. Genetically lowered 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations were associated with higher ovarian cancer susceptibility.
